Anthropic’s new FlashProve system shows that provable inference for large language models is becoming practical.  

The core result is a zk‑SNARK proof generated at roughly 110 tokens per second for a 1,024‑token request, with each proof occupying about 19 MiB.  

FlashProve runs on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU, uses 4‑bit quantized weights, and achieves a 70–95× speedup over prior open‑source approaches.  

“The proof hides the model’s weights while binding the computation to the committed architecture.”  

This matters because it gives enterprises a cryptographic guarantee that a specific, vetted model produced an output, addressing trust gaps in regulated AI deployments.  

The performance numbers rely on a 400 billion‑parameter mixture‑of‑experts model and integer arithmetic during the prefill phase, which may not generalize to all model architectures.  

How will you incorporate provable inference into your AI security strategy?  

Full breakdown with sources: https://buildwithsaksham.in/blog/progress-on-provable-inference-for-large-language-models
